mbm-2776.clue: My favorite treasure is on the way out.
mbm-2776.quote: Our museum has an old bronze shoe scraper by the exit. A century of boots polished one horse's nose gold. I take my sketchbook there after the grand rooms and their velvet ropes.

mbm-2777.clue: My screen has a little lighthouse keeper.
mbm-2777.quote: I wrote a program that flashes one pixel in the top corner after my homework timer runs out. Then I drew a tiny lighthouse beneath it. Now someone always signals when it's time to stretch.

mbm-2778.clue: My three lemons have names in pencil.
mbm-2778.quote: I learned a new juggling pattern by writing my cousins' initials on three lemons. Calling the names aloud made the catches come easier. We had rather a lot of family lemonade after practice.

mbm-2779.clue: The voice from downstairs knows my part.
mbm-2779.quote: I practice harmony above a tailor's shop. One evening I stopped at the tricky bar and a voice from the stairs hummed the missing note. The tailor got a front-row seat at our next concert.

mbm-2780.clue: I wrote all night for one small smile.
mbm-2780.quote: My first program drew my father's face with twelve blue squares. When I pressed the space bar the corner of his mouth moved up one pixel. He kept pressing it like a doorbell.

mbm-2781.clue: The golf pencil has racing stripes.
mbm-2781.quote: I put two stripes of tape on the little pencil so my grandpa could find it in the grass. It looks fast. We still take three tries to get through that miniature train tunnel.

mbm-2782.clue: My ham set lives in a bread cabinet.
mbm-2782.quote: I fitted shelves into the empty cabinet from our old bakery. The call cards stand where the loaves used to cool. My operator friend insists the signal has a particularly good crust.

mbm-2783.clue: My serve has to clear the shadow first.
mbm-2783.quote: As kids we had no net, so we served over the line where a wall shadow met the sand. By evening the wall had a terrific reach. We can still play a whole match with just a ball and some sun.

mbm-2784.clue: The shoe brush sits by the record player.
mbm-2784.quote: I polish my dance shoes while I listen to the week's new records. By the third track I can tell which pair to wear. My oldest shoes always pick the quickest song.

mbm-2785.clue: I saved one sleeve with the paint on it.
mbm-2785.quote: We repainted my sister's room in yellow when we were teenagers. Her old paint shirt goes across the quilt like a ray of sunlight. That room has changed hands but we still have its first bright afternoon.

mbm-2786.clue: Two shells mark my popping crease.
mbm-2786.quote: Our beach cricket pitch slopes a little toward the sea. I bury two white shells to line up the crease. By lunch the waves have given the home side six more inches.

mbm-2787.clue: I date our board games by the coins.
mbm-2787.quote: We use foreign coins as pieces. Lift the lid and you can see where our family traveled that summer. My favorite is the cheap copper one that crossed the table in Grandma's first win.

mbm-2788.clue: We named the practice stone after a bus.
mbm-2788.quote: There is one gray curling stone that takes the widest route to the house and still gets there. My partner calls it the local. We leave early and enjoy all its stops.

mbm-2789.clue: My painting starts with five minutes of shadow.
mbm-2789.quote: I put the canvas on my balcony and trace the fern's shadow before the morning wind comes up. I paint whole imaginary forests around those fronds. The one real tree is a very small potted fern.

mbm-2790.clue: My leather notebook has a window.
mbm-2790.quote: I cut a little round hole in the cover to show the color of the first page. When I finish a story I slip in a different sheet. My friends ask what color this month has been.

mbm-2791.clue: My hook makes a very slow garden.
mbm-2791.quote: I crochet one leaf each time my houseplant puts out a real one. The plant is winning. I hung the yarn vine on the other side of the kitchen window so they can climb toward each other.

mbm-2792.clue: Our bocce court has a quiet corner.
mbm-2792.quote: My neighbor's apricot tree leans over one end of the court. When fruit starts to drop we move the pallino a little. Nobody minds if the game stops for an apricot.

mbm-2793.clue: I record the faces watching the tape.
mbm-2793.quote: At anime club we sketched each other during the most surprising scene. My picture shows three wide mouths and a hand reaching blindly for popcorn. Nobody in the drawing is looking at me.

mbm-2794.clue: A little flick of blue woke up the whole page.
mbm-2794.quote: I was sketching a dull brown bird when it spread one brilliant blue wing in the sun. My pencil case didn't have the color. I cut a speck from the bus ticket and glued it where the wing had been.

mbm-2795.clue: I play the note beneath the floorboards.
mbm-2795.quote: Our rehearsal room has a floorboard that hums with my bass. I place a glass of water on it when we're tuning up. If the little rings meet the rim, we have our first note.

mbm-2796.clue: My summer reading comes with a sundial.
mbm-2796.quote: I set my ice water between the sun and my book. The glass throws a bright wandering spot across the page. When it reaches the bottom margin I switch to the shaded bench for another chapter.

mbm-2797.clue: My museum visit left tracks in the sand.
mbm-2797.quote: A museum volunteer poured a tray of damp sand beside a display of old sandals. We tried replicas to see what the soles would leave. My print had a herringbone pattern. My friend's looked like a tray of little biscuits.

mbm-2798.clue: We leave a seat for the seagull.
mbm-2798.quote: The top board of our volleyball bench is no wider than a fin. A gull lands there every week to watch the ball. Nobody leaves sandwiches near our most dedicated fan.

mbm-2799.clue: Our waltz took two feet on the pedals.
mbm-2799.quote: At the garden ballroom we had one light bulb and a bicycle dynamo. Dad pedaled for our first waltz while I danced. Halfway through we swapped places without stopping the tune. His smile was worth every turn of the pedals.

mbm-2800.clue: One end of the pool smells like oranges.
mbm-2800.quote: The swim team coach peeled an orange at the finish end every Saturday. I haven't had his stopwatch on me in years, but a whiff of orange peel can still make me kick a little harder.
